intro: Searching for a farm solicitor near you usually means something practical has come up with the family farm, whether that's a tenancy question, a partnership arrangement or a sale you're considering. You want someone who knows agricultural law and is close enough to understand the local picture. We introduce you to a suitable UK solicitor who quotes you directly, so you can compare what's on offer.
need_heading: What people searching for a farm solicitor near me usually need
need_lead: Farm solicitors deal with the legal side of land, family arrangements and the future of the farm business.
needs: You are thinking about selling part or all of the farm and need to understand the legal steps, including any tenancy or boundary issues.
Your family farming partnership has never been put into a formal agreement and you want to sort out how decisions and profits are shared.
A dispute has arisen with a tenant or a neighbour over land, access or a tenancy agreement and you need advice on where you stand.
You are planning to hand the farm on to the next generation and want to organise wills, succession and ownership properly.
You want to diversify the farm, perhaps with a new building or a change of use, and need to know whether planning permission is required.
context_heading: Checking who can help with your farm matter
context: Solicitors in England and Wales are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority, and you can check an individual or firm on the SRA's register. In Scotland the regulator is the Law Society of Scotland, and in Northern Ireland it is the Law Society of Northern Ireland. Regulated firms must hold professional indemnity insurance and have a complaints procedure.

The word "lawyer" is not protected on its own, so it is worth confirming that whoever handles your matter is a solicitor, a chartered legal executive or another authorised professional. Reserved activities such as conducting court litigation and certain probate and conveyancing work can only be carried out by authorised people.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the farm and the land involved, including whether it is owned, tenanted or a mix of both.
Explain what has prompted you to look for a farm solicitor now, such as a sale, a dispute or a family conversation about succession.
Say whether there is an existing partnership agreement, tenancy agreement or will that you need reviewed.
Mention any planning or diversification plans you have, even if they are early ideas.
Give the county or area where the farm is located so we can introduce you to a solicitor familiar with the local context.
Let us know if you are acting for yourself or on behalf of a family partnership or other business structure.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the farm solicitor
questions: What experience do you have with agricultural tenancies and family farming partnerships?
How will you keep me informed about progress and costs as the matter develops?
Will you be the person handling my matter, or will it be passed to a colleague?
What information or documents should I gather before we begin?
Are there any time limits or upcoming deadlines I should be aware of?
What is your approach to resolving disputes, and when might mediation be appropriate?

faqs.q: Do I need a solicitor who specialises in farm matters?
faqs.a: Farm solicitors understand the particular issues that arise with agricultural land, tenancies and family partnerships. Using someone with that background can help you avoid common pitfalls. We introduce you to a solicitor who deals with farm work, and you can ask about their experience directly.

faqs.q: Can iComply tell me how much a farm solicitor will cost?
faqs.a: No, we do not set or quote fees. The solicitor you are introduced to will quote you directly, price on application, so you can discuss costs before instructing them. It is sensible to ask about likely costs and how they will be charged at that point.

faqs.q: What should I do if I am unsure whether someone is a qualified solicitor?
faqs.a: You can check the Solicitors Regulation Authority's register for England and Wales, the Law Society of Scotland, or the Law Society of Northern Ireland, depending on where you are. The word "lawyer" is not protected, so it is worth confirming that the person is a solicitor or another authorised professional before sharing sensitive information.

faqs.q: Can a farm solicitor help with planning for the next generation?
faqs.a: Yes, farm solicitors often advise on succession planning, including wills, partnership agreements and ownership structures. They can help you have conversations about the future of the farm and put arrangements in place. It is best to start early so there is time to consider all the options.
